questions.q: What does Discovery actually do, per this lesson?
options: Automatically scans a network to find devices and software, and uses what it finds to create or update CMDB records
Lets an administrator type CI data into a form faster than before
Replaces the need for a CMDB entirely
Only works on CIs that were already entered manually
questions.explain: Discovery is an automated scanning capability — the alternative to typing every CI in by hand.

questions.q: Why doesn't manual CI entry, on its own, scale — per Chapter 1's honest data-quality discussion?
options: Data entered and maintained entirely by hand goes stale the moment something changes and nobody updates the record
Manual entry is actually more accurate than any automated approach, forever
The CMDB table structure physically rejects more than a few hundred manually entered records
Manual entry was banned starting in Chapter 3
questions.explain: Manual entry is accurate the day it's typed in, but nothing keeps it current once reality changes — that's the staleness problem Discovery addresses.

questions.q: What role does the MID Server play in Discovery, connecting back to course 7?
options: It's the customer-installed application that actually carries out Discovery's scans on the target network, since ServiceNow's cloud instance can't reach it directly
It has no connection to Discovery at all
It replaces the ServiceNow instance entirely during a Discovery scan
It only matters for REST integrations, never for Discovery
questions.explain: Course 7 established that a MID Server bridges the gap between the cloud instance and a network it can't see directly — Discovery is one of the specific jobs that requires it.

questions.q: What kind of data is Discovery genuinely good at keeping current?
options: Infrastructure-level facts — what exists, its specs, and what software is installed on it
Which business owner should be assigned to a CI
The correct lifecycle status governance policy for a service
Discovery cannot reliably find any data at all
questions.explain: Discovery excels at infrastructure-level facts; ownership and lifecycle governance still depend on the processes from Chapter 3 and Chapter 5.

questions.q: Why is it inaccurate to call Discovery a complete fix for the CMDB data-quality problem from Chapter 1?
options: Discovery doesn't guarantee correct ownership, business service relationships, or lifecycle status on the CIs it creates — that still requires governance
Discovery doesn't actually find any real infrastructure data
Discovery only works once and never runs again
Discovery was deprecated in favor of manual entry
questions.explain: Discovery keeps infrastructure data current with much less manual effort, but the governance layer from Chapter 3 and Chapter 5 is still what keeps that data meaningful.
